cards.title: Re-adding an equivalent name preserves shopping intent
cards.body: When Rice is already marked needed, adding “ rice ” reuses Rice and preserves its needed mark. Only an explicit change to the needed mark changes the household’s shopping decision.
cards.tests:
“Names are trimmed, and a case-insensitive match on the full supplied name reuses the existing item.”
“The household controls that mark as a shopping decision; it is not inferred from stock.”
cards.why: Accepting protects the existing shopping decision when a duplicate is added accidentally. Resisting could treat adding a pantry supply as replenishment and clear its needed mark, saving an explicit action, but would make adding silently reinterpret shopping intent.
